inconsistencies: #36114 explicitly absorbs and supersedes #35358: they solve the same external-signer trust problem, so #36114 should be reviewed first and #35358 closed or rebased on top of it.

Four overlapping rebroadcast-privacy PRs (#36398, #36380, #34533, #36330) address the same leak with incompatible policies: #36398 (only rebroadcast own txs) is the broadest and should be decided first; #34533 (route rebroadcast through private broadcast) and #36330 (suppress rebroadcast entirely under -privatebroadcast) directly contradict each other; #36330 is marked NO MERGE and #36380 adds a user-facing switch over whichever policy wins.

Dependency chain whose review order matters: #32895 (version records) and #33033 (SQLite statement RAII) are prerequisites for #33034 (transactions table), which in turn unblocks #27865 (no-longer-spendable TXO tracking, the measured speedup). #33033 was assessed two bands below the work it unblocks; raised to P2.

Three RPC-input crash fixes of the same class had been split across P1/P2/P3: #35989, #36339 and #36342. #35989 stays P1 because it is also reachable from a plain -keypool setting during ordinary descriptor import; the other two are now both P2.

#35742 and #36420 both fix duplicate-key detection in Miniscript descriptors (multipath branches vs x-only parity) and touch adjacent code in descriptor.cpp; they should be reviewed together to avoid conflicting fixes.

#36070, #35918 and #36143 are all prerequisites for the multisig wizard tracked in #35645; they are ranked together so the wizard backend is evaluated as one design rather than three isolated helpers.
Silent Payments: #35302 (sending) depends on base PR #35301, which is not in this list, and is best reviewed after #32966 (receiving); #32966 itself is gated on upstream libsecp256k1 work (#1799).
#19460 depends on #10102 (and #29409); reviewing it before multiprocess lands gives no standalone wallet benefit.

#35317 fixes a genuine silently-ignored RPC option, but reviewers propose closing it in favour of a project-wide snake_case transition issue; the underlying bug should not be lost if the PR is closed.
result.notes: The category splits cleanly: a small P1 core of fund-safety and silent-correctness defects (external signer trust, load-time assertion crash, rescan/import balance bugs), a broad P2 of corruption/backup-handling, privacy-of-broadcast, measured performance work and major features, a long P3 of real-but-deferrable fixes, features and refactors, and a P4 tail of test-only and cosmetic changes. The main cross-PR issues are the four competing rebroadcast PRs, the #35358/#36114 duplication, and the #32895/#33033 -> #33034 -> #27865 chain, whose review order was not reflected in the per-PR scores.
